outputs.L1: Systems and methods are disclosed for extending a programming language with a set of extensions using a strict meta-model. Embodiments provide a set of interfaces that enable the synthesis of a schema. Syntax is introduced into an existing programming language to facilitate the construction of schematized data objects. A schema processor module translates a schema representation into new keywords, and a document generator module receives the set of keywords and produces output in a selected form. When code comprising the keyword extensions is parsed, data structure nodes represent keyword actions as a set of functions and implement the corresponding function calls using the original metadata. A keyword definition comprises a name, an action to be performed at parse time, and an action to be performed at runtime. By default, the parse-time action injects a function call into the code, while the runtime action calls the function.
outputs.L2:
Disclosed are systems and techniques for augmenting a programming language with extensions governed by a strict meta-model. In various embodiments, interfaces are provided through which a schema can be synthesized. New syntax is added to an existing language so that schema-based data objects can be created. A schema-processing module converts a schema representation into a collection of new keywords, which a document-generation module then uses to generate output in a chosen format.

When source code containing these keyword extensions is parsed, nodes in the data structure model the keyword operations as functions and execute the associated function calls using the original metadata. Each keyword definition includes a keyword name, an operation performed during parsing, and an operation performed at runtime. By default, parsing inserts a function call into the code, while the standard runtime behavior invokes that function.
outputs.L3:
A strict meta-model extends a programming language through a clearly defined set of extensions. Within this model, interfaces support schema synthesis, while additional syntax enables developers to construct data objects that conform to those schemas.

A schema processor translates schema representations into new keywords that become part of the programming language. These generated keywords can then be used by a document generator to produce output in a selected format.

Each keyword definition specifies both parse-time and runtime behavior. By default, the parse-time action injects a function call into the program, and the runtime action executes that call using the original metadata associated with the keyword.
outputs.L4:
A strict meta-model extends a programming language with new, schema-driven syntax while preserving a clear relationship between each language construct and the metadata from which it was derived. Rather than defining every keyword and behavior manually, the system uses interfaces to describe the available structures and their constraints. These interfaces are synthesized into schemas that serve as the authoritative definitions of the language extension.

A processor then translates the schemas into concrete keyword definitions. During this translation, schema fields, types, relationships, and annotations are mapped to the grammar and semantic rules required by the host language. Because the process is schema-driven, generated keywords remain consistent with their source interfaces, and invalid or incomplete constructs can be rejected according to the strict rules of the meta-model.

The generated definitions can include actions for both parsing and execution. Parse-time actions determine how a keyword is recognized, validated, and represented in the resulting syntax tree or intermediate form. Runtime actions specify what should happen when that representation is evaluated. By default, the processor implements these actions by injecting function calls into the parsed representation and arranging for those functions to be invoked during execution. Alternative actions may be supplied when a keyword requires different parsing or runtime behavior.

A generator completes the pipeline by producing only the requested outputs. Depending on the configuration, this may include grammar fragments, keyword implementations, runtime support code, metadata, documentation, or other derived artifacts. Selective generation avoids emitting unnecessary components while ensuring that all selected outputs are based on the same schemas.

As a result, parsed code does more than record that a keyword appeared in the source. It retains or references the original metadata associated with that keyword and uses that information to implement its behavior. The schema therefore connects interface definitions, generated syntax, parse-time validation, and runtime execution, allowing language features to be declared once and reproduced consistently throughout the system.
outputs.L5:
### Systems, Embodiments, Syntax

A system is never only an abstract arrangement. It becomes visible through its embodiments: a city organized into streets, a body coordinated by nerves, a computer animated by circuits, or a society structured through institutions. Each embodiment gives material form to relationships that might otherwise remain invisible.

Syntax governs how the elements within a system can be combined. In language, it arranges words into meaningful sentences. In programming, it defines valid instructions. In architecture, it appears in the relationship between walls, openings, and spaces. Syntax is not the content itself; it is the set of rules and patterns that enables content to take shape.

Yet embodiments can also transform syntax. A rule expressed in speech behaves differently when written, coded, performed, or built. Material conditions introduce limitations, possibilities, errors, and interpretations. For this reason, systems are not fixed structures imposed upon passive forms. They evolve through the interaction between organizing rules and their concrete realization.

To understand a system, then, we must examine both its syntax and its embodiments. Syntax reveals how parts are connected; embodiment shows what those connections become in practice. Meaning emerges between the two—between structure and matter, possibility and expression, order and lived reality.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing systems and methods for extending a programming language through a strict meta-model, schema-generated keywords, and parse-time and runtime actions.
counterfactuals.output: Systems and methods are disclosed for extending a programming language using a strict meta-model. The meta-model defines permissible language constructs, relationships, attributes, constraints, and associated processing behavior in a machine-readable schema. An extension processor validates an extension definition against the meta-model and automatically generates corresponding keywords, grammar elements, parsers, documentation, and programmatic interfaces. Each generated keyword may be associated with one or more parse-time actions and runtime actions. Parse-time actions are invoked during lexical, syntactic, or semantic analysis to transform source representations, populate an intermediate model, enforce constraints, or emit diagnostics. Runtime actions are invoked during execution to perform operations represented by the corresponding language constructs. A dispatcher binds parsed constructs to the actions according to type information and behavioral declarations contained in the schema. The strict meta-model limits extensions to defined structural and behavioral contracts, thereby enabling independently developed extensions to interoperate without modification of a core compiler or interpreter. In some implementations, schema versioning, dependency resolution, namespace isolation, and generated validation logic permit extensions to be composed while preserving deterministic parsing and execution. The disclosed techniques reduce manually authored parser code, maintain consistency among syntax, semantics, and tooling, and provide a controlled mechanism for adding domain-specific capabilities to an existing programming language.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

This enables schema-based data to be expressed, transformed, and rendered consistently across different languages and document types.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent abstract about a schema processor and document generator that extend an existing programming language, represent keyword actions as function-call nodes, and execute them using original metadata.
counterfactuals.output: A computer-implemented system extends an existing programming language to support schema processing and document generation. A parser receives a source definition containing native language constructs and schema-specific keywords and generates an intermediate representation in which actions associated with the schema-specific keywords are represented as function-call nodes compatible with the existing programming language. Original metadata corresponding to the keywords, including source location, identifier, ordering, annotation, and contextual information, is preserved in association with the function-call nodes. A schema processor evaluates the intermediate representation using an execution engine of the existing programming language and invokes corresponding keyword functions based on the preserved metadata. Results of the keyword functions are combined to construct a schema model, validate input data, and generate a document according to the schema model. By translating keyword actions into executable function-call nodes while retaining original metadata, the system provides language extensibility, diagnostic traceability, and document generation without modification of the underlying language runtime.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
